review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no simp attributes, so I looked at how it handles `simp`-style rewriting of `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor` at finite places. I read the two competing lemmas, `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl` (@[simp], in FiniteExtensionPrincipalDivisor.lean) and `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl_eq_finitePlaceOrder` (not simp, in TorsionExhaustiveGcdDivisorBound.lean). A grep found about 30 uses of the latter across 11 files, which I only counted and did not read one by one. I did not check whether other files rely on the default-simp expansion by `_inl`. So the claim that demoting `_inl` is safe is unverified, and I hedged it in the proposed change. I also did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour. I did not report the duplicated huOrder/hvOrder blocks, because they are a proof-structure matter rather than a simp-interface problem.

findings.problem: Two rewrite rules compete for the same left-hand side `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor K L x (.inl q)`. The default simp lemma `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl` is @[simp] and rewrites it to `finitePlaceOrder q ((ratFuncFiniteIntegralClosureFractionRingEquiv K L).symm x)`. That form goes through an equivalence and is not the form the finite-place lemmas consume. The lemma `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl_eq_finitePlaceOrder` gives the form the consumers want, `finitePlaceOrder q x`, but it is not simp. As a result this file, and about 30 occurrences across 11 files, must write `simpa only [finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl_eq_finitePlaceOrder]` by hand and cannot use plain `simpa`. This file does it six times (lines 159, 163, 168, 176, 180, 185). Plain `simp` would instead produce the `.symm`-equiv form, which does not match the `finitePlaceOrder q u` hypotheses.
findings.proposed_change: Make `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl_eq_finitePlaceOrder` the canonical simp lemma by adding @[simp] to it. Remove @[simp] from `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl`, or keep it as a non-simp lemma that callers cite explicitly, so the two rules do not compete. Callers that currently use `simp only [finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor_inl, ...]` already name the lemma and would keep working. Callers that rely on plain `simp` to expand it need to be checked. The six `simpa only [...]` calls here could then become plain `simpa using ...`, or be shortened.
findings.benefit: Expressions `finiteExtensionPrincipalDivisor K L x (.inl q)` would normalise to the `finitePlaceOrder q x` form the finite-place lemmas use. Proofs would no longer need an explicit `simp only` override of the default simp set. The default simp set would be consistent with what the downstream finite-place case lemmas expect.
